scope: Source-side verification of the picks the deployed CS2 dashboard already publishes: every active row's pick replayed from its published probabilities, every cited source link checked against the official host, the identity chain behind the researched 1082792 row re-checked against Hotspawn, Polymarket and HLTV, the live coverage gap reconciled against a captured lobby, and the executive-summary / phone findability contract verified. No pick was generated and no number was changed.
method: Read only what this repository publishes. snapshot.json (the 2026-10-25T23:03:48Z publish) and index.html (the executive summary built from it) were read directly; every active row's two probabilities were re-derived arithmetically from its own analysis.probabilities and pick_index, and every row's analysis.source_url was required to be https and to name an official source rather than a Hotspawn page or an HLTV fan-vote surface. The 1082792 identity chain was re-checked against three independent sources read through the platform page fetcher: Hotspawn fixture 1082792, Polymarket event cs2-hotu-the9-2026-10-31 and HLTV match 2399437. The live lobby and scheduled-fixtures API were captured at 2026-10-26T00:48-00:50Z and reconciled with the snapshot's upcoming set. Nothing was inferred; a value that could not be confirmed was left as a flagged limitation rather than filled in.

items.area: Executive summary prices 1082792 while snapshot.json's featured layer leaves it blank
items.finding: The deployed executive summary shows Hotspawn fixture 1082792 (HOTU vs The Huns, Moscow Cyber Games 2026, starts 2026-10-31T09:00:00Z) as Pick HOTU, HOTU 87.0% / The Huns 13.0%, badged 'Researched' + 'Market line', observed 82-92 / 8-18, cited to Polymarket event cs2-hotu-the9-2026-10-31. The same publish's snapshot.json records the identical fixture with analysis null, pick_index null and limitations 'Hotspawn best-of format is unverified' and 'The Huns: multiple Valve rosters share this name; identity is unresolved', and with featured.unresolved = 1. So two layers of the same publish disagree about whether this fixture is priced.
items.handling: The identity chain behind the researched row was verified against three independent sources read first-hand, and it holds: Hotspawn 1082792 starts 2026-10-31T09:00:00Z; Polymarket eventStartTime is 2026-10-31T09:00:00Z with outcomes 'HOTU' and 'The Huns Esports' and a description naming the Moscow Cyber Games Playoffs Semifinal 1 between HOTU and The Huns Esports; HLTV match 2399437 is 'HOTU vs. The Huns at GLuck Moscow Cyber Games 2026', Best of 3 (LAN), Semi-final. The row is therefore a prediction-market money line with a researched identity - not a Hotspawn crowd percentage and not an HLTV fan vote. The featured layer is unresolved because its exact-name matcher does not silently alias sponsor or abbreviated names ('The Huns' != 'The Huns Esports', Polymarket's slug is 'the9'). No number was changed here; the chain is recorded so a reader can re-open all three links.

items.area: 1082792 limitation 'Hotspawn best-of format is unverified' is superseded by two external sources
items.finding: snapshot.json records the limitation 'Hotspawn best-of format is unverified; left blank.' for 1082792. That is a true statement about Hotspawn's payload, which sends best_of null and series_format null for every current fixture, but it is not true of the fixture: Polymarket publishes the event as '(BO3)' and HLTV lists 'Best of 3 (LAN)'.
items.handling: Flagged for the pipeline that writes the limitation text, not changed here. The limitation describes the Hotspawn record rather than the match; a reader who opens the three links in R01 can see the format. Left as a labelled limitation rather than inferred, which is the project's rule.

evidence.detail: Event title ends '(BO3)' and the description calls it 'the Counter-Strike Semifinal 1 match between HOTU and The Huns Esports'.
HLTV lists 'Maps - Best of 3 (LAN)' and '* Semi-final'.

items.area: Live Hotspawn coverage gap: nine open fixtures absent from the deployed snapshot
items.finding: At 2026-10-26T00:48-00:50Z the live Hotspawn CS2 lobby lists 19 open fixtures and the scheduled-fixtures API returned records through index 81, while the deployed snapshot (generated 2026-10-25T23:03:48Z, inventory 72 observed 23:03:30Z) serves 10 upcoming. The nine Hotspawn lists but the snapshot does not serve are 1079201, 1081159, 1079202, 1081160, 1079203, 1093218 (NODWIN Clutch Series #13) and 1081162, 1081163, 1081164 (CCT Europe 2026 Series #12). Every one is tier b, lock_offset_sec 360, offered_points 3, and carries a very low Hotspawn total_picks (2-8, against 39-49 on the covered fixtures) - the low-tier academy/second-division fixtures the brief says must still get a pick.
items.handling: Recorded as a dated observation, not as a collector defect. scripts/collect.py reads the fixture API wholesale with no client-side pagination and no date-window filter, so it cannot have dropped these nine; the snapshot's own inventory recorded 72 records at 23:03:30Z and the API returned more at 00:50Z, so the fixtures were added to Hotspawn's schedule between those two reads. The four-hour publisher re-collects on every refresh and will serve them once it runs; a publisher run was already in flight when this was written. No pick was invented for them here.

evidence.detail: Live lobby read 2026-10-26T00:48Z: 19 open CS2 pick'ems cards, eight closing soon and eleven upcoming.
The scheduled-fixtures API read at 2026-10-26T00:50Z; its tail chunks end hasMore=false and carry the nine ids above.
The deployed snapshot: generated_at 2026-10-25T23:03:48Z, 72 inventory records at 23:03:30Z, 10 upcoming.

items.area: Executive summary counts complete-layer picks, snapshot.json counts featured-layer picks
items.finding: The executive summary headline reads '10 active Hotspawn CS2 fixtures in this snapshot, 10 with a directional pick - 8 from an external betting line, 2 from a research model - and 0 explicitly unresolved'. The same publish's snapshot.json featured layer records featured.picked = 9 and featured.unresolved = 1 (the unresolved fixture is 1082792, which the summary prices through the researched complete layer). The two counts answer different questions and the landing page does not say which layer it is counting.
items.handling: Flagged for the owning renderer, not changed here. The summary does disclose the split in its own words ('the featured exact-name method left 1 fixture(s) without a pick. Each now carries a researched estimate from a named source'), so a careful reader is not misled, but the headline number and the snapshot's unresolved count are different views of the same publish.
